extracted.intended_audience: computational-linguistics and multimodal-ML researchers building/using humor-detection datasets and models
extracted.subtask_description: Creation, annotation, and evaluation of a multilingual stand-up-comedy dataset for automatic laughter/humor detection framed as word-level sequence labeling; includes ASR-based cleaning, candidate selection, manual test annotation, and baseline modeling protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition and inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The StandUp4AI dataset is composed of 3,617 stand-up videos in 7 languages (English, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Hungarian, Czech) totaling ≈334 hours; on each channel, videos from YouTube Shorts and videos where more than one comedian appeared were excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect videos from curated channels (Table 1). Exclude shorts and multi-comedian videos to keep performances coherent; report per-channel/language counts (videos, hours, words, laughter labels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter annotation framing (word-level sequence labeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not frame humor/laughter detection as a binary sequence classification; instead label at the word level so each word receives a binary tag indicating whether laughter occurs right after it and before the end of the next word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framing enables continuous prediction throughout a joke and anticipatory prediction (predicting laughter before it happens in model observations). Use word-aligned labels rather than end-of-sequence punchline detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label creation procedure for laughter segments
rubrics_metrics.description: For each laughter segment with start t0 and end t1, find the 'start' word whose timing window either overlaps or immediately follows t0, and the 'end' word around t1; if both boundaries fall on the same word label that word positive, otherwise tag all words in between as positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use word timestamps from ASR outputs (after correction) to map time-based laughter segments to word indices so models can predict start/stop of laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic laughter-detection pipeline baseline choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary off-the-shelf acoustic laughter detector used: Omine et al. (2024) model; unsupervised baseline used: FunnyNet framework (Liu et al., 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run multiple detectors for comparison; use state-of-the-art supervised detectors as well as unsupervised baselines to evaluate gains from ASR-based enhancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASR tools and expected ASR error characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts and timestamps are produced using two ASR systems: Whisper (Radford et al., 2023) and WhisperX (Bain et al., 2023). Real word errors are small (examples: French word errors <1.0%, timestamp errors ~2.0%; English word errors <0.5%, timestamp errors ~0.1%), with most errors caused by similar pronunciations and missing fillers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect variation by language and dialect (e.g., dialects like Mexican/Chilean Spanish challenge ASR). Inspect common misrecognitions (e.g., 'qu’on' vs 'con') as they may change semantics; plan corrections for timestamp perturbations near laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASR-based timestamp correction (intersection method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct timestamp errors around laughter by aggregating outputs of Whisper and WhisperX: search for longer-in-time words and check for intersections between transcripts; when found, keep the begin and end timestamps of the intersection to insert a new laughter in the resulting transcript and remove the intersection from neighboring word timestamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method addresses merging of laughter into neighboring words (Whisper tends to merge with next word; WhisperX with previous). Use intersection timestamps to create candidate laughter events and fix erroneous word time windows (see Table 6 example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic candidate laughter selection and manual validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate candidate outbursts from ASR-corrected transcripts; manually annotate candidates in a subset (50 videos) to determine real laughter vs other events, then train a classifier (RandomForest) on these examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use manual labels on candidates to bootstrap a classifier that filters false-positives from acoustic detection; manual annotation of a representative subset is required to train this filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acoustic feature set for candidate classifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract a comprehensive acoustic feature set including temporal (duration, voiced ratio, burst count, temporal centroid), energy (rms mean/std/slope, energy at 90th percentile), spectral (bandwidth, rolloff at 85/95%, flatness, contrast, centroid), pitch (median, std, HNR), modulation energy (4–12 Hz), chroma (1–12), MFCCs (1–13) and first/second derivatives (delta, delta2 MFCCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a rich, multi-type feature set (temporal/energy/spectral/pitch/chroma/MFCC) to distinguish laughter from fillers/claps/noise. Librosa is used to extract features in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-processing rule: discard very short audio segments
rubrics_metrics.description: All audio segments with duration shorter than 0.5 seconds are discarded and classified as 'other' (not considered in model evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short bursts under 0.5s are excluded from candidate evaluation to avoid spurious detections; apply this threshold prior to classifier training/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate classifier model and hyperparameter tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a RandomForest binary classifier to distinguish laughter from non-laughter. For hyperparameter tuning use 15% of the dataset for validation; tuned parameters included n_estimators, max_depth, and min_samples_split with optimal values reported as n_estimators=50, max_depth=13, min_samples_split=2; run multiple iterations varying train/test splits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform many iterations (the paper used 200) varying training/testing splits while consistently holding out 15% for validation; report confidence intervals for precision/recall/F1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test set manual annotation protocol and reliability target
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a manually annotated test set of 67 videos (~10 per language) annotated with precise timestamps to 0.1s using audio and Audacity; annotate twice to compute Krippendorff's α using a distance metric based on IoU with threshold 0.2; reported inter-annotator agreement α = 0.91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate at high temporal precision (0.1s), double-annotate for reliability, and compute Krippendorff's alpha with an IoU distance (threshold 0.2) to quantify agreement. Manually check ASR outputs to ensure label-word alignment for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metric for acoustic laughter detection (IoU-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate acoustic laughter detections using sequence-overlap metrics such as Intersection-over-Union (IoU) with a recommended threshold of 0.2 to consider a prediction positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IoU≥0.2 for hit/miss decisions when comparing predicted laughter segments to manual ground truth; report precision, recall, and F1 at that IoU threshold (the paper reports these comparisons across methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation choice for word-level sequence labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate sequence-labeling models with classification metrics (precision, recall, F1) on word-level labels rather than sequence-classification frameworks (e.g., do not rely on rigid sequence-evaluation tools like seqeval) because the task is predicting laughter at word boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground metrics on word-level predictions (binary per-word) rather than temporal IoU; clarify evaluation unit (word) and report standard classification metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence preprocessing for model training (max length and stride)
rubrics_metrics.description: Train sequence-labeling transformers with a maximum sequence length of 512 tokens and use a stride of 128 tokens when cutting from the same monologue to ensure past context is preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When splitting long monologues maintain overlap (stripe/stride) to keep context for tokens near chunk boundaries; choose max_length=512 with stride=128 as an effective configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling/training protocol for sequence labeling baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tune pretrained transformers (xlm-roberta-base) with Adam optimizer, 10 epochs, learning rate 1e-5. Use standard libraries (transformers, torch) and report classification metrics per language and model type (monolingual vs multilingual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent training hyperparameters and report multilingual vs monolingual comparisons; make experimental environment and library versions explicit for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of cleaned/enhanced labels on model performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Models trained on the ASR-enhanced (cleaned) set of laughter labels achieve higher performance than models trained on raw off-the-shelf-laughter detections; training on cleaned data is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply ASR-based enhancements (timestamp corrections and candidate filtering) to produce cleaner weak labels before model training to improve downstream sequence-labeler F1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of auxiliary visual features (optional for multimodal work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Release visual features extracted from videos (Action Units via LibreFace, poses via MMdetection/MMpose, camera-angle changes via PySceneDetect) though not used in the current unimodal baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide extracted visual descriptors in the released dataset so future multimodal experiments can integrate them; document which videos were discarded for visual extraction failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Report limitations including unimodal focus in initial baselines (only textual/unimodal models), not modeling laughter intensity, dialectal ASR errors (e.g., Chilean/Mexican Spanish), and reliance on YouTube videos which may be deleted; do not distribute raw video/audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list limitations in dataset/model papers, plan normalization/intensity annotation in future work, and mention dialect effects on ASR. Use metadata/annotations only to mitigate copyright concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and data distribution policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute only extracted annotations and transcripts — not the original videos — for strictly non-commercial, academic research; provide a dedicated contact email for GDPR-related removal requests; prohibit redistribution or commercial exploitation of the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State legal/ethical rationale (fair use, InfoSoc Directive) and include attribution requirements to comedians; enforce non-commercial license and provide mechanisms to honor removal requests under privacy regulations.
